papers.title: The relationship between gait kinematics and cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gait impairment and cognitive dysfunction are common in Parkinson's disease (PD), but the interaction between these domains, particularly under dual-task walking, is less well characterised. OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between gait parameters and cognitive domains in PD during single- and dual-task walking. METHODS: 50 individuals with PD and 21 age-matched healthy controls completed single-task walking and two dual-task conditions, involving naming animals and performing serial subtraction by seven. Gait was recorded using an electronic pressure-sensitive walkway (Zeno™, ProtoKinetics) and analysed for velocity, step length, step time, step length variability, and step time variability. Participants completed cognitive assessments of processing speed, executive function, memory, and language. Associations between gait parameters and cognitive domains were assessed for significant correlations. RESULTS: In participants with PD, executive dysfunction, measured by the Trail Making Test Part B (TMT-B), was differentially associated with increased step length variability during dual-task walking. Less robust findings were observed for single-task conditions or other cognitive domains. CONCLUSION: Executive dysfunction appears to relate to impaired control of gait variability under dual-task conditions in PD, consistent with a key role for attentional-executive resources in maintaining stable gait. These findings may help focus future work on specific dual-task interferences relevant to PD progression and gait decline.

papers.title: Detection of candidate acoustic biomarkers for Parkinson's disease using an explainable machine learning composite spectrogram approach.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Speech abnormalities are common in Parkinson's disease (PD), and machine learning (ML) offers a potential framework for objective and scalable speech-based diagnostics. This study introduces an explainable ML pipeline that leverages a novel vowel articulation-based composite input to detect PD and identify candidate phoneme-level biomarkers. METHODS: Two publicly available datasets of PD speech recordings were analyzed. Sustained vowel articulations were converted into log-mel spectrograms either individually or as a composite image by vertically concatenating a set of vowels per subject. Processed spectrograms were used to train ML models, with performance assessed using repeated random subsampling with five participant-level 80:20 splits and bootstrapped area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest trained on conventional acoustic features served as baselines. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to quantify model attention across vowel regions. RESULTS: A total of 150 participants (49.3% PD) were included. After adjustment for age, sex, and dataset, cepstral peak prominence and harmonics-to-noise ratio were significantly higher in PD, particularly for the vowel /u/. The ML model achieved an average AUROC of 0.895 using individual vowels and 0.890 using the composite input (p CONCLUSION: The proposed explainable composite spectrogram approach enabled identification of a candidate vowel-level biomarker while retaining high classification performance. Concordance between ML and acoustic analyses suggests the potential of explainable ML in PD speech assessment, pending validation in larger cohorts and other languages.

papers.title: Concussion history and the range of chronic impairments.
papers.abstract: Mild traumatic brain injury (concussion) affects approximately 50 million people worldwide each year, and up to half of affected individuals develop persistent symptoms. However, the range of long-term impairments associated with concussion remains incompletely characterized. We conducted an exploratory retrospective analysis of the Fox Insight Parkinson's disease (PD) study including 2602 participants with history of concussion > 6 months prior, and 2602 age- and sex-matched participants without concussion history. By using symptom questionnaires validated for PD we extended the scope beyond those symptoms often studied in concussion. Specifically, binary logistic regression models assessed associations between concussion history and 58 outcomes spanning cognitive, psychiatric, motor, autonomic, sleep, and instrumental activities of daily living. Analyses included several demographic variables, comorbidities, and medications as covariates, were corrected for multiple comparisons, and complemented by sensitivity analyses. Participants had a mean age of 63.9 years and 54.7% were female. Concussion history was associated with significantly higher odds of impairments across all assessed domains, including cognition, psychiatric symptoms, motor function, autonomic function, sleep, and instrumental activities of daily living. Despite this, only 5% of participants with concussion history reported a diagnosis "post-concussion syndrome". Exclusion of individuals with PD or other sensitivity analyses did not substantially change results. While causality cannot be inferred, these findings suggest that concussion may contribute to chronic neurological burden over longer time frames and across more symptom domains than currently recognized and support the need for longitudinal studies to establish causal pathways and inform long-term clinical follow-up.

papers.title: The R56Q Mutation in αB-crystallin Enhances its Ability to Suppress Fibrillization of α-Synuclein A53T.
papers.abstract: Alpha-B crystallin is a member of the small heat shock protein family. Unlike αA crystallin, which is found exclusively in the lens of the eye, αB crystallin is present in many tissues of the body, where it is induced by stress. Alpha-B crystallin prevents the aggregation of various cellular proteins. In addition, it inhibits amyloid-like aggregation of α-synuclein, a protein involved in the development of human neurodegenerative diseases called synucleinopathies. In this paper, we have shown that αB-crystallin with the R56Q mutation (αB-Cr_R56Q) exhibits enhanced ability to suppress amyloid aggregation of α-synuclein A53T (αSynA53T, a mutation associated with early-onset Parkinson's disease) compared to the wild-type αB-crystallin (αB-Cr_wt). By data of dynamic light scattering, the hydrodynamic diameter of αB-Cr_R56Q molecule decreases compared to the αB-Cr_wt (12.5 and 17.3 nm, respectively). Analysis of tryptophan fluorescence spectra shows that binding of αSynA53T to αB-Cr_R56Q causes the transition of the N-terminal domain to the oligomer surface, while in the case of αB-Cr_wt, the N-terminal domain is buried inside the oligomer. Analysis of literature data and our experimental data allowed us to assume that the R56Q mutation disrupts interactions between the N-terminal domain and the core α-crystallin domain of the adjacent subunit that maintain the oligomeric structure of the molecule. This may lead to oligomer remodeling and the formation of smaller oligomers. At the same time, the disruption of these interactions releases additional binding sites for αSynA53T, which leads to more efficient suppression of αSynA53T amyloid transformation.

papers.title: TAK-341 in Multiple System Atrophy: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is a rapidly progressing and fatal α-synucleinopathy characterized by parkinsonism, ataxia, and severe autonomic dysfunction, with no available therapies to prevent or slow its progression. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated efficacy, pharmacodynamics, and safety of the anti-α-synuclein antibody TAK-341 in participants with possible or probable MSA. METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, phase 2 study, 158 participants randomly assigned to TAK-341 or placebo (saline) received treatment intravenously every 4 weeks. Primary endpoint was change from baseline to week 52 on the modified Unified Multiple System Atrophy Rating Scale (UMSARS) part I with TAK-341 versus placebo. Analyses were performed using a mixed-effect model with a repeated-measurement approach, using observed-case data. RESULTS: Sixty-five participants completed treatment with TAK-341 and 63 with placebo. Baseline characteristics were balanced between study arms. The majority of participants had a diagnosis of probable MSA (72.6% and 71.6%, respectively). Evaluation of the modified UMSARS part I score at week 52 did not show a statistically significant difference (mean change: TAK-341, 5.1 [SD: 4.42]; placebo, 5.2 [SD: 5.05], P = 0.961). No significant differences were observed in the secondary efficacy outcomes or magnetic resonance imaging assessments between study arms. However, target engagement by TAK-341 was demonstrated by a statistically significant reduction (mean percentage change from baseline) of -38.1% in cerebrospinal fluid levels of free α-synuclein at week 52 versus 0.3% with placebo (P = 0.001). TAK-341 was well tolerated, and treatment-emergent adverse events were comparable in both study arms. CONCLUSIONS: Based on these findings, participants with possible/probable MSA did not exhibit differences in disease progression with TAK-341 versus placebo. © 2026 Takeda Pharmaceuticals and The Autho

papers.title: Lipid Droplet Remodeling at the Glia-Neuron Interface: Metabolic Sinks, Flux Traps, and Therapeutic Pitfalls in Neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neurological decline, metabolic dysfunction, and chronic neuroinflammatory changes. Dysregulated lipid handling has emerged as an important component of these processes, but the functional significance of lipid droplets (LDs) remains strongly context-dependent. Here, we review LD biogenesis, turnover, and cell type-specific functions in the central nervous system (CNS) and critically evaluate evidence linking LD remodeling to neurodegeneration. Transient LD formation can buffer excess or oxidation-prone lipids and support metabolic adaptation, whereas persistent lipid retention in the setting of impaired lysosomal, mitochondrial, or lipid-export capacity is associated with cellular dysfunction. We compare human tissue data, genetic evidence, LD-specific perturbations, pharmacological studies, and experimental models across Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and Huntington's disease (HD). Particular attention is given to microglial lipid-associated states, neuron-glia lipid transfer, monogenic disorders of lipid handling, and apparently opposing outcomes of LD manipulation in different disease contexts. Rather than treating LD accumulation as a universal pathogenic mechanism, we propose LD remodeling as a candidate metabolic-inflammatory convergence state whose functional consequences depend on cell type, lipid composition, turnover capacity, and disease stage. Translational strategies should therefore prioritize direct measurements of LD flux, demonstration of CNS target engagement, and biomarker-guided patient and disease-stage selection. We further define experimental findings that would support or falsify the proposed convergence model.

papers.title: Aptamers in neurodegenerative disease: Systematic review and computational analysis of aptamer-protein interactions.
papers.abstract: Aptamers are short single-stranded nucleic acids or peptides that bind molecular targets with high affinity and specificity, making them promising tools for diagnostics and therapeutics. In neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, there is an urgent need for sensitive biomarkers and effective disease-modifying therapies. Here, we present a systematic review and meta-analysis of aptamer technologies in neurodegenerative diseases and evaluate trends in aptamer design, molecular targets, chemical modifications, and applications. We identified 139 studies comprising more than 177 aptamers targeting diverse disease-associated molecules. Systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX)-based approaches predominated, with DNA aptamers substantially more common than RNA, peptide, or synthetic xeno nucleic acid (XNA) aptamers. papers.title: Practical Clinical Examination Framework for Parkinsonism: Integrating Bedside Phenomenology and Biomarkers.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review presents a practical framework for the work-up of patients with parkinsonism, including an overview of the appropriate use and interpretation of imaging and biomarkers in this patient population. RECENT FINDINGS: In recent years, new biomarkers have been developed to detect alpha-synuclein in cerebrospinal fluid, skin, and other tissues, and alpha-synuclein biomarkers are now available in clinical practice for the work-up of Parkinson's disease and related disorders. In addition, research is ongoing into neuroimaging techniques to distinguish Parkinson's disease from atypical neurodegenerative parkinsonisms. Important questions remain for the practicing clinician regarding when to pursue advanced neuroimaging or biomarker analysis. In this review we present an overview of the diagnostic work-up of patients with parkinsonism, including a discussion of neurologic exam findings and phenomenology, and an update on available imaging, fluid, and tissue biomarkers. We further provide an assessment of the appropriate clinical contexts in which to consider pursuing imaging and biomarker assessments and how to appropriately interpret the results of such tests.

papers.title: Methylene Blue Attenuates Plasma Neuron-Specific Enolase Elevation Induced by Annona muricata L. Leaf Extract in Wistar Albino Rats.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Annona muricata PATIENTS AND METHODS: Thirty-six rats were acclimatized and randomized into six groups (3 males + 3 females per group): normal saline (2mL/day; negative control), selegiline (0.5 mg/kgBW/day; positive control), 0.5% dimethyl sulfoxide (0.1 mL/day; vehicle control), and three treatment groups receiving methylene blue (1 mg/kgBW/day), garlic extract (300 mg/kgBW/day), and turmeric extract (200 mg/kgBW/day). After 7 days of pretreatment, all animals received soursop extract (200 mg/kgBW/day) for 21 days while continuing assigned treatments. Blood was collected on days 0, 7, 14, 21 and 28 for plasma NSE quantification by ELISA. Data were analyzed by ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc tests (p<0.05). RESULTS: Plasma NSE followed a U-shaped trajectory in all groups, declining to a nadir at day 14 and rising thereafter. The late rise was greatest in the normal-saline group (day-28 mean 145.00 ng/mL). Methylene blue and selegiline significantly attenuated the endpoint elevation (88.60 and 87.60 ng/mL, respectively; both p<0.001 versus normal saline) and did not differ from each other. Garlic and turmeric produced intermediate reductions. Three-way mixed ANOVA showed significant main effects of day (F(4,96)=33.69, p<0.001), treatment (F(5,24)=7.82, p<0.001) and a day × treatment interaction (F(20,96)=3.56, p=0.002). papers.title: Neuroimmune pharmacology of dextromethorphan/bupropion (Auvelity): Mechanistic insights into microglial regulation, inflammasome suppression, and therapeutic translation.
papers.abstract: Neuroinflammation is increasingly recognized as a central pathogenic mechanism in major depressive disorder and diverse neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury, and neuropathic pain. Persistent activation of microglia and astrocytes, excessive cytokine production, inflammasome activation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity can collectively disrupt neuronal homeostasis and promote disease progression. Dextromethorphan/bupropion (Auvelity) is a fixed-dose combination that integrates N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonism, sigma-1 receptor agonism, monoaminergic modulation, and cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibition, thereby producing sustained dextromethorphan exposure and multimodal pharmacological activity. Preclinical studies of dextromethorphan and bupropion individually provide mechanistic evidence suggesting potential effects on microglial activation, Toll-like receptor 4 and nuclear factor kappa B signaling, inflammasome activity, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function. However, direct evidence demonstrating that these neuroimmune effects are produced by the fixed-dose combination remains limited. This review examines the pharmacological basis of dextromethorphan/bupropion, its potential interactions with major neuroimmune pathways, and available experimental and clinical evidence. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing direct combination evidence from component-specific findings and mechanistic extrapolation. The translational relevance of reported mechanisms is considered across major neuroinflammatory disorders, with attention to pharmacokinetic exposure, clinical evidence, biomarker assessment, and future precision neuroimmunopharmacological strategies. papers.title: Freezing of Gait in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy: An Underreported Phenomenon.
papers.abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a clinically heterogeneous 4R tauopathy in which gait impairment is a defining and diagnostically relevant feature across all recognized subtypes. This narrative review evaluates the available quantitative evidence on gait pathology in PSP, with a particular focus on freezing of gait (FOG) assessment. A structured search of the MEDLINE PubMed database and Cochrane Library covering the past 20 years identified 16 eligible studies for inclusion. Across these studies, PSP was consistently characterized by reduced gait velocity, shortened stride length, decreased cadence, and prolonged double support time, with greater impairment than in Parkinson's disease (PD). Increased gait variability-particularly stride and step time variability-emerged as a sensitive marker of supraspinal locomotor dysregulation and longitudinal disease progression. Dynamic gait stability was measurably reduced, and gait asymmetry was reported in a subset of studies, though it remains systematically undercharacterized. Critically, none of the 16 reviewed studies employed a standardized FOG assessment or video-based FOG rating, and the subtype PSP with progressive gait freezing was consistently underrepresented with small patient numbers. This review identifies the absence of standardized FOG assessment as a fundamental methodological gap in the current literature, and highlights quantitative gait analysis as a promising tool for differential diagnosis, subtype assignment, and disease progression monitoring in PSP.

papers.title: Directional deep brain stimulation outside Parkinson disease: systematic review and tremor-focused meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Directional deep brain stimulation (dDBS) enables current steering, which may potentially improve therapeutic efficacy and reduce stimulation-induced adverse effects. Although dDBS has been extensively studied in Parkinson disease (PD), evidence in non-Parkinson indications remains limited. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed the evidence comparing directional and omnidirectional DBS in indications other than PD. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were systematically searched in January 2026 according to PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included at least one patient implanted with a clinically available dDBS lead and reported postoperative outcomes in non-PD indications. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for tremor studies with sufficient quantitative data. RESULTS: Forty-one studies involving 309 patients and 456 implanted leads were included. In patients with tremor, meta-analysis showed that dDBS was associated with a wider therapeutic window than omnidirectional stimulation (SMD 1.83, 95% CI 0.76-2.90; p = 0.0408; I2 CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence for dDBS outside PD remains limited and heterogeneous. The strongest evidence exists for tremor, where dDBS was associated with a wider therapeutic window and comparable symptom control, although the certainty of evidence is low. Evidence for dystonia, pain, and psychiatric disorders remains insufficient to draw firm conclusions. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome measures and longer follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Investigating Co-Speech Gesture Production in People with Parkinson's Disease: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Motor and linguistic deficits in people with Parkinson's Disease (PwP) have been well documented. Gestures are thought to arise from embodied simulations of motor and linguistic representations during speech, yet the use of gesture in the context of speech, or co-speech gestures (CSGs), in PwP is unclear. Therefore, this scoping review aimed to assess what methods have been used to study CSGs in PwP, whether their use is different to healthy controls, and consider implications for cognitive theory and rehabilitation in Parkinson's. Five electronic databases were consulted, and from an initial 605 records, ten were identified. Most studies showed no significant difference in gesture rate or types of gestures used between PwP, with mild to moderate symptoms, and controls. There was, however, some inconsistency which may reflect methodological differences, such as modality of the information to be communicated and the communicative context. Additionally, some findings suggested that PwP may be relying more on visual third person representations rather than motoric simulations when depicting actions through gesture. Although the number of studies was quite small, findings that PwP can still produce different CSG types and use visual compensation to match gesture rate indicate that these are a potential target in communicative rehabilitation. Furthermore, PwP's use of CSGs also provide a method to explore cognitive representations in language and motor function. Ultimately, further research is needed, such as in neuroimaging for PwP's gesture use, longitudinal design, and in those with more severe motor symptoms, to explore changes over disease progression.

papers.title: Freezing of gait and cognition are associated with white matter microstructure of the corpus callosum in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Freezing of gait (FOG) is a common phenomenon in Parkinson's Disease (PD). People with PD and FOG (PD + FOG) present more severe executive dysfunction compared to those without FOG. White matter (WM) microstructure integrity of the corpus callosum has been implicated in both FOG and cognitive impairments in PD. Executive dysfunction likely contributes to FOG; however, whether FOG severity and executive dysfunction in PD are associated with the same corpus callosum WM microstructure deficits remains unknown. This pilot study aimed to identify associations among FOG severity during turning-in-place (FOG-ratio), executive function, and corpus callosum WM microstructural integrity as measured by fractional anisotropy (FA). Twenty-six subjects with PD + FOG underwent magnetic resonance diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and were assessed for FOG severity (FOG-ratio during turning-in-place) and executive function (Frontal Assessment Battery-FAB). Spearman's rank correlation coefficients were calculated, and Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Results showed that FOG-ratio was negatively associated with FAB scores (r = - 0.59, P = 0.003, corrected). FA in the genu and body of the corpus callosum were negatively associated with FOG-ratio (r = - 0.63, P = 0.001 corrected; r = - 0.48, P = 0.014 corrected) and positively associated with FAB scores (r = 0.45, P = 0.017 corrected; r = 0.41, P = 0.025 corrected). This pilot study shows that quantitative measures of FOG severity during turning and executive function deficits are associated with corpus callosum microstructure.

papers.title: Expanding the clinical and geographical spectrum of PARK-LRRK2 p.(Asn1437His): first report in a Swiss family.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pathogenic variants in the LRRK2 gene represent the most common monogenic cause of Parkinson's disease. Individual variants differ in frequency, geographical distribution and genotype-phenotype associations. Here, we report a Swiss family with multiple affected individuals carrying a very rare ROC-domain variant and provide a comprehensive characterisation of their clinical phenotype. CLINICAL FINDINGS: Age at onset was earlier than typically reported for PARK-LRRK2. Leg tremor was frequently the initial presenting symptom, followed by the development of an asymmetric akinetic-rigid syndrome with a clear dopaminergic response. Constipation was commonly reported, whereas significant cognitive symptoms were not evident. Notably, despite the high penetrance of the variant, disease progression was relatively mild. PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Genetic testing identified a heterozygous missense variant in the LRRK2 gene (c.4309A>C, p.(Asn1437His)), classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG criteria. CONCLUSION: The present work expands both the geographical distribution of this rare ROC-domain variant and suggests that it may be associated with earlier onset but not necessarily greater disease severity. Continued characterisation of rare LRRK2 variants is essential for refining genotype-phenotype correlations and supporting emerging targeted therapies.
